arxiv-2109-05889.title: Nonlocal Patch-Based Fully-Connected Tensor Network Decomposition for Remote Sensing Image Inpainting Thanks: This work was supported in part by the National Natural Science Foundation of China under Grant 61876203 and Grant 12071345, in part by the Project for Applied Basic Research of Sichuan Prov
arxiv-2109-05889.creator: Wen-Jie Zheng, Xi-Le Zhao, Yu-Bang Zheng, Zhi-Feng Pang
arxiv-2109-05889.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Wen-Jie Zheng, Xi-Le Zhao, Yu-Bang Zheng, Zhi-Feng Pang. Remote sensing image (RSI) inpainting plays an important role in real applications. Recently, fully-connected tensor network (FCTN) decomposition has been shown the remarkable ability to fully characterize the global correlation. Considering the global correlation and the nonlocal self-similarity (NSS) of RSIs, this paper introduces the FCTN decomposition to the whole RSI and its NSS groups, and proposes a novel nonlocal patch-based FCTN (NL-FCTN) decomposition for RSI inpainting.

arxiv-2502-16833.title: An Exploratory Study on How AI Awareness Impacts Human-AI Design Collaboration
arxiv-2502-16833.creator: Zhuoyi Cheng, Pei Chen, Wenzheng Song, Hongbo Zhang, Zhuoshu Li, Lingyun Sun
arxiv-2502-16833.description: Abstract . The collaborative design process is intrinsically complicated and dynamic, and researchers have long been exploring how to enhance efficiency in this process. As Artificial Intelligence technology evolves, it has been widely used as a design tool and exhibited the potential as a design collaborator. Nevertheless, problems concerning how designers should communicate with AI in collaborative design remain unsolved.

arxiv-2505-00712.title: A Goal-Oriented Adaptive Sampling Procedure for Projection-Based Reduced-Order Models with Hyperreduction
arxiv-2505-00712.creator: Calista Biondic, Siva Nadarajah
arxiv-2505-00712.description: Abstract Projection-based reduced-order models (PROMs) have demonstrated accuracy, reliability, and robustness in approximating high-dimensional, differential equation-based computational models across many applications. For this reason, it has been proposed as a tool for high-querying parametric design problems like those arising in modern aircraft design.

arxiv-2506-15339.title: DeVisE: Behavioral Testing of Medical Large Language Models
arxiv-2506-15339.creator: Camila Zurdo Tagliabue, Heloisa Oss Boll, Aykut Erdem, Erkut Erdem, Iacer Calixto
arxiv-2506-15339.description: Abstract Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used in clinical decision support, yet current evaluation methods often fail to distinguish genuine medical reasoning from superficial patterns. We introduce DeVisE ( De mographics and Vi tal s igns E valuation), a behavioral testing framework for probing fine-grained clinical understanding.

arxiv-2507-22372.title: Leveraging Caliper and Benchpark to Analyze MPI Communication Patterns: Insights from AMG2023, Kripke, and Laghos
arxiv-2507-22372.creator: 1 st Grace Nansamba, 2 nd Evelyn Namugwanya, 3 rd David Boehme, 4 th Dewi Yokelson, 5 th Riley Shipley, 6 th Derek Schafer, 7 th Michael McKinsey, 8 th Olga Pearce, 9 th Anthony Skjellum
arxiv-2507-22372.description: Abstract We introduce “communication regions” into the widely used Caliper HPC profiling tool. A communication region is an annotation enabling capture of metrics about the data being communicated (including statistics of these metrics), and metrics about the MPI processes involved in the communications, something not previously possible in Caliper.

pmc-12488541.title: Exercise and Heart Rate Variability in Chronic Musculoskeletal Pain: A Systematic Review
pmc-12488541.creator: Timo Meus, Julie Van Eetvelde, Iris Meuwissen, Mira Meeus, Daniel Boullosa, Annick Timmermans, Jonas Verbrugghe
pmc-12488541.description: BackgroundChronic musculoskeletal pain (CMP) is a prevalent condition associated with significant disability. Emerging evidence suggests that autonomic dysfunction, reflected by heart rate variability (HRV), may play a role in the pathophysiology of CMP and could be responsive to exercise interventions. This systematic review aims to evaluate the effects of exercise on HRV in persons with CMP.

pmc-12526951.title: Wireless Inertial Measurement Units in Performing Arts
pmc-12526951.creator: Emmanuel Fléty, Frédéric Bevilacqua
pmc-12526951.description: Inertial Measurement Units (IMUs), which embed several sensors (accelerometers, gyroscopes, magnetometers) are employed by musicians and performers to control sound, music, or lighting on stage. In particular, wireless IMU systems in the performing arts require particular attention due to strict requirements regarding streaming sample rate, latency, power consumption, and programmability.

pmc-12557344.title: The Role of Intraoperative Neurophysiological Monitoring in Intracranial Cavernous Malformation Surgery: A Narrative Review
pmc-12557344.creator: Mei Shao, Qi-Yang Huai, Jian-Wei Song, Fu-Qiang Wang, Yan-Na Li, Xia Li, Feng-Ling Wang
pmc-12557344.description: Cavernous malformations, also known as cavernous hemangiomas or cavernomas, are abnormal vascular lesions that can occur in various parts of the body, including intracranially. Surgical resection is often the preferred treatment for symptomatic or high-risk lesions located in eloquent or critical brain or spinal cord regions.

pmc-12604330.title: Esophageal obstruction by mediastinal seroma after laparoscopic repair of a giant hiatal hernia: a case report
pmc-12604330.creator: Štěpán-Ota Schütz, Jaroslav Pažin, Tereza Husárová, Radek Pohnán
pmc-12604330.description: BackgroundHiatal hernia is increasingly prevalent in the Western population. Its incidence increases with age and morbid obesity and is higher in females. Symptomatic hiatal hernias, particularly grade IV, are associated with significant morbidity and severe symptoms, and often necessitate acute surgical intervention.

pmc-13325621.creator: Laleh Jalilian, Navid Manafi, Matthew Scott Vandiver, Paul Lukac, Achuta Kadambi
pmc-13325621.description: BackgroundIn intensive care unit (ICU) settings, structured team-based communication, such as multidisciplinary rounds, handoffs, and goals-of-care discussions, is foundational to high-quality care.
